assumptions.choice: Support zone defined as close price in [support_level, support_level*1.015] i.e. within 1.5% above the ~$170.00 level, checked on the closing price for consistency with the close-based stop-loss rule
assumptions.reason: Spec gives only a single approximate support price (~$170.00), not a zone width, so a tolerance band had to be chosen to operationalize 'drops to a support zone'

assumptions.choice: N = 10 bars for both the rising-trend entry filter and the falling-trend alternative exit
assumptions.reason: Spec requires N > 1 but leaves the exact lookback unspecified; 10 hourly bars (~1.5 trading days) was chosen as a concrete, moderate value

assumptions.choice: Implemented as a required entry condition (close > SMA60 and close > SMA120), not merely optional
assumptions.reason: Spec phrases it as 'a condition can be introduced,' but it is listed under 'Conditions for Entering a Long Position,' so for fidelity it is enforced as a required filter

assumptions.choice: Fixed +3% from entry price (middle of the stated 2-5% range); implemented via close() against entry_price
assumptions.reason: Spec gives a percentage range but no concrete number, so the midpoint was chosen as a single deterministic threshold

assumptions.choice: Not implemented; only the percentage-based take-profit alternative is used
assumptions.reason: infeasible - the spec supplies no numeric resistance level (unlike the ~$170.00 support), and none can be derived from OHLCV data alone

assumptions.choice: Not implemented; strategy trades purely on price/SMA conditions
assumptions.reason: infeasible - spec explicitly states this factor 'is difficult to automate' and no fundamentals/ownership data are available in the OHLCV feed

assumptions.choice: Risk 1.5% of current broker equity (midpoint of stated 1-2%) per trade; size = floor(risk_amount / (entry_close - support_level)), skip entry if size resolves to 0 or stop distance is not positive
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly requires stop-loss risk to be capped at 1-2% of capital rather than leaving sizing unstated, so the canonical default plain buy() does not apply and an explicit risk-based share count was computed from the entry price's distance to the ~$170.00 stop
